content.user_title: Generate Clear Changelogs from Git Commits
content.value_statement: Release notes are slow when commit messages are technical or inconsistent. This skill turns git history into clear changelogs for customers, teams, and release channels.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes commits from a selected period or between versions.
Groups changes into features, improvements, fixes, breaking changes, and security notes.
Rewrites technical commit messages into user-facing release language.
Filters internal changes such as refactoring, tests, and maintenance work.
Formats changelogs for public release notes, app stores, and product updates.
Can follow a project-specific CHANGELOG_STYLE.md guide.
limitations: Requires access to relevant git history or commit summaries.
Output quality depends on commit message quality and project context.
Generated changelogs should be reviewed before publication.
The skill provides guidance, not a standalone automated release pipeline.

use_cases.title: Prepare Version Release Notes
use_cases.description: Turn commits between versions into a polished changelog for a product release.

use_cases.title: Write Customer Product Updates
use_cases.description: Convert weekly development work into a readable update for customers and stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Maintain Public Changelog Pages
use_cases.description: Create consistent entries for CHANGELOG.md, GitHub releases, or product update pages.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a recent release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a changelog from commits since the last release. Use clear language for customers.

prompt_templates.title: Date Range Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a weekly or monthly update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a changelog for commits from the past week. Group changes by features, improvements, and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Versioned Release Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured prompt for a named version.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create release notes for version 2.5.0. Highlight customer impact and call out breaking changes separately.

prompt_templates.title: Style-Guided Changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a changelog for commits since v2.4.0. Follow CHANGELOG_STYLE.md and exclude internal maintenance commits.

output_examples.input: Create a changelog from commits since the last release.
output_examples.output: A release note with sections for new features, improvements, and fixes, written in customer-friendly language.

output_examples.input: Generate product updates from the past week.
output_examples.output: A concise weekly update that summarizes customer-visible changes and omits internal development noise.

output_examples.input: Create app store release notes for version 2.5.0.
output_examples.output: A short release summary focused on user benefits, fixed issues, and any required upgrade notes.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root or provide complete commit history.
Specify the date range, version range, audience, and target release channel.
Review the generated changelog for accuracy before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated notes without checking product facts.
Do not include sensitive internal commits in public release notes.
Do not use vague commit ranges when a specific version or date range is available.

faq.question: Does this skill read git commit history?
faq.answer: It is designed to analyze commit history or commit summaries supplied in the working context.

faq.question: Can it create customer-facing release notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It rewrites technical changes into clearer language for customers and product audiences.

faq.question: Can it follow our changelog style guide?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a CHANGELOG_STYLE.md file or clear formatting rules in the prompt.

faq.question: Will it remove internal engineering work?
faq.answer: It can filter routine refactoring, tests, and maintenance when they are not relevant to users.

faq.question: Is the output ready to publish automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review the generated changelog for accuracy, completeness, and product messaging.
